title: S3 Tables Namespace definition
description: Schema for a single namespace definition file at s3tables/namespaces/<name>.yaml. One file describes exactly one namespace. The file name has no functional meaning - identity comes from metadata.name - but keeping them aligned is recommended.

name.description: Namespace name. This is the field that identifies the namespace - not the file name or file location. The actual AWS namespace name may be prefixed as edp_<environment>_<namespace> depending on the enable_namespace_prefix Terraform variable - write the unprefixed name here either way.

owner.description: Team or individual responsible for this namespace. Informational only - not consumed by Terraform.

description.description: Human-readable description of what this namespace is for. Informational only - not consumed by Terraform.

environments.description: Which environment(s) this namespace (and its tables) should be deployed to, and optionally which IAM roles may produce into it there. Keyed by environment name; each value is either {} (namespace/tables only, no producer) or { iamRoles: [...] } (a producer role + dedicated Athena workgroup edp-<env>-tables-<namespace> is provisioned for the listed role ARNs to assume). If this key is omitted entirely, it defaults to all four environments with no producer in any of them - equivalent to writing dev: {}, test: {}, uat: {}, prod: {}. When present, only the environments listed here are used - there is no default-fill for environments left out.

^(dev|test|uat|prod)$.description: Per-environment configuration. Empty object means the namespace (and its tables) are created here with no producer.

iamRoles.description: IAM role ARNs that may assume the EDP namespace producer role edp-<env>-s3tables-producer-<namespace> Terraform provisions for this namespace in this environment. Omit this key entirely (or omit the environment) for consumer-only access - the namespace and its tables are still created, but no producer role is.
